title: Iron-air battery round-trip efficiency
bottleneck: Iron-air batteries promise roughly 20 dollars per kWh storage for 100-hour duration using rust chemistry, but round-trip efficiency is low, potentially below 50 percent, and power density is poor: they discharge slowly and recharge slower. Low efficiency means massive renewable overbuild to compensate for losses, and slow response limits grid services revenue. The technology is unproven at commercial scale.
why_it_blocks: Ultra-cheap storage that wastes half its energy is only viable with near-free surplus renewables. Efficiency determines whether iron-air is a breakthrough or a curiosity.
current_state: Form Energy is building its first commercial iron-air factory with utility contracts. Field efficiency and durability data are pending. Utilities signing early contracts are betting that ultra-low capital cost outweighs efficiency losses, a wager that field data has not yet settled.
